column1: # vibejuel1651 key: the two ciphers of Peder Vibe's letters to Peder Juel, 1649-1655 (Rigsarkivet, TKUA Sverige, unit 261583), CC BY 4.0
# (Brice Dudout, Europe chiffree, 2026). Recovered from the letters themselves: the partial interlinear decipherment of the time on
# N. 319 (image 78) gave the system; the rest was read with it. Vibe names both ciphers in clear (image 62, 11 Jan 1649): the new
# alphabet ("dett ny Alphabet") is to follow, and meanwhile he writes "wed woris forige gamble Ciffres".
# Both ciphers are shift ciphers with a shift chosen per word. A cipher word = OPENER + BODY. The opener (first number, 1-3 or 24-39)
# gives a shift k; each body number n stands for the letter of rank n - k (1-based). In the body, 32/33/34 stand for 1/2/3.
# section G - "gamle Ciffres" (old cipher): letters of 1649-1650, the slip f. 318 (July 1651?) and N. 330 (20 Sep 1651).
#   23 letters, i = j, u = v/w, CYCLIC (rank taken mod 23): a with k = -1 is written 23; a with k = -2 is 22.
#   The 21st letter is x (perplex, sex); the hand of 1649-51 has no w.
#   25 letters a ... u w x y z oe (w = 21, x = 22, y = 23, z = 24, oe = 25), i = j, not cyclic.
#   Opener table (the same in every letter read): 24-29 -> 0; 30-34 -> 1; 35-39 -> 2; 1-3 -> 3.
#   A word may be split in pieces, each with its own opener (eders = 3.8.7 + 30.6.18.19).
# section C - nomenclator: two- to four-digit numbers standing between the words (211, 228, 257, 422, 872 ...; in 1655 up to 1771).
#   None is identified by any key. Two are defined in clear by Vibe (image 80, 6 Jan 1653): "sub N 349" and "N 561" are to be added
#   to the cipher; the names that follow are hard to read (Wranghel? and Wranghel's mother?), so they are given here as probable only.
# Columns: section, cipher (letter value at k = 0, or opener range), value, note.
